key_insight: ENGINE uses high-dimensional probes to correct low-dimensional zeroth-order updates, reducing the trade-off between gradient variance and information loss in LLM fine-tuning.
engineering_relevance: It transfers variational multiscale ideas from computational mechanics to memory-efficient LLM optimization.
method: Treat low-dimensional and full-parameter spaces as resolved coarse and unresolved fine scales.
Alternate between scales through a multigrid-style V-cycle.
Inject fine-scale information into coarse updates to reduce variance and curvature-induced bias.
evidence_signal: On standard LLM benchmarks, the abstract reports higher accuracy and faster convergence than existing zeroth-order methods, with up to 2.61× speed-up in forward passes and no additional peak memory overhead.
watch_item: The theoretical guarantees depend on assumptions, and the abstract does not specify benchmark-level variability or practical subspace-selection requirements.
paper_title: ENGINE: Endogenous Variational MultiScale Optimization for Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning
